crops.d: Warm-season cereal usually grown with standing water or alternate wetting and drying.
p: Climate/season: varies by region (kharif/rabi); check local calendar
Soil: puddled clay or clay-loam soils retain water
Seed: use healthy, locally adapted, certified organic or untreated seed
Nutrients: compost, green manure (e.g. dhaincha), biofertilizers per soil test
Weeds: timely hand/mechanical weeding, water management
Rotation: follow with a pulse to restore soil nitrogen
Common mistake: continuous flooding or crowded planting that encourages disease

crops.d: Cool-season cereal grown on well-drained loam soils.
p: Season: cool/rabi season; sowing dates vary by region
Soil: well-drained loam; avoid waterlogging
Nutrients: well-matured compost and green manure preceding crop
Rotation: rotate with legumes
Check local varieties and recommendations

crops.d: Fast-growing cereal that responds to good soil organic matter and moisture.
p: Season: kharif or rabi depending on region
Intercrop with pulses where suitable
Nutrients: compost and legume rotation, based on soil test
Watch for fall armyworm; scout early and consult extension office

crops.d: Hardy, drought-tolerant grains suited to low-rainfall areas and poorer soils.
crops.k: millet ragi jowar bajra korra chirudhanyalu
p: Often grown rainfed; choose locally adapted types
Mix with pulses as intercrop for stability
Low input needs; compost improves yield stability

crops.d: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen and improve soil when rotated with cereals.
crops.k: pulses legumes gram pigeonpea lentil pappu
p: Well-drained soil; avoid waterlogging
Rhizobium culture (approved biofertilizer) may help; follow product label
Rotate with cereals
Common mistake: over-irrigation causing root rot

crops.d: Short-duration crops needing fertile, well-drained soil and steady moisture.
p: Use compost-rich beds and mulching
Rotate across plant families (e.g. avoid tomato after brinjal)
Scout weekly for pests and diseases
Use physical barriers and traps before any treatment

crops.d: Perennial fruit trees and plants that need long-term soil care.
p: Site and variety must match local climate
Mulch basins; compost applied around the root zone
Prune for airflow and sanitation

crops.d: Groundnut, sesame, sunflower and similar crops.
p: Well-drained light soils for groundnut
Rotate with cereals
Store dry to avoid mould

crops.d: Chilli, turmeric, ginger and others needing rich organic soil.
crops.k: spice chilli turmeric ginger mirapa pasupu
p: Rich, well-drained soil with plentiful compost
Mulching conserves moisture
Use healthy planting material to avoid rhizome/seed-borne disease

Incorporate at the right growth stage before flowering

fertilizers.d: Crops grown to protect and feed the soil between main crops.

Choose species suited to your season

Follow label directions; wear protection

Store cool; follow label instructions

Record what you find and when

Use a government or accredited lab
